A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial restructuring and experimental revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulation and learning experiments on Hamiltonian and dissipative systems, including benchmark comparisons, trajectory-count studies, and latent-initialization experiments.

after.justification: v2 reports original benchmark experiments, multi-domain learning results, component ablations, and analyses of learned bases and latent representations.

M1.justification: v2 extends v1's rank-one hypernetwork-generated update to variable-rank matrix-factor updates, including MR(5), and introduces locality penalties on latent codes and hypernetwork parameters. Crucially, v1's MR factorization corresponds to v2's SVD formulation: its ReLU, orthogonality, and sparsity mechanisms already appeared in v1 Appendix F and are not new components.

E1.justification: Kepler and the two-gas-container system are removed, including their appendix experiments. Mass-spring, pendulum, Duffing, and DNO remain. v2 also adds a distinct multi-domain scenario in which one shared base network learns across the three conservative systems, replacing the exclusively separate-system evaluation scope of v1.

E2.justification: The external comparator set remains Scratch, MAML, Reptile, ANIL, Shift, and FW. After matching v1 MR to v2 SVD and retaining RO, corresponding benchmark comparisons add variable-rank MR and restricted-rank SVD variants, including SVD(5) and DNO's SVD(3). FW's identification as CODA does not introduce another baseline.

E3.justification: The reported split changes from 70/20/10 training/validation/test systems to 70/10 training/test, and the base MLP changes from four to two layers. v1 describes q-only training with estimated p; v2 describes simulated q,p with finite-difference derivatives. Visualizations change from 100-shot to 300-shot adaptation, and new interpolation experiments use a 50/50 split. Exact settings remain partly inconsistent: v2's main text specifies SiLU, while Appendix G retains tanh and 100 adaptation steps.

E4.justification: v2 adds parameter-efficiency comparisons, locality and orthogonality tests, rank and sparsity sweeps, learned-basis analyses, latent-dimension sensitivity, and latent-space visualization/interpolation. The average-versus-zero initialization experiment is retained and revised, rather than newly introduced. Conversely, v1's trajectory-count sweeps and two-gas-container component and expressivity analyses disappear.

E5.justification: Main conservative-result tables change their stated aggregation from seven runs to five. Initialization comparisons newly report standard deviations, and locality experiments describe five runs per regularization setting with aggregation across settings. Both versions nevertheless retain an implementation statement specifying three repetitions, so the actual run counts cannot be fully reconciled.

E6.justification: Benchmark values and rankings are extensively revised, with additional variant, ablation, and multi-domain results and removed Kepler/TGC entries. For example, pendulum FW trajectory error changes from 0.200 in v1 Table 1 to 0.1065 in v2 Table 1. Revised DNO results explicitly report Reptile NaNs and ANIL divergence. These are results under changed protocols, not established same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: v2 adds Proposition 3.1 on local dimension under a constant-rank assumption, its proof, and Proposition D.1 explicitly proving modulation's compatibility with structure preservation. Appendix A also introduces asymptotic hypernetwork parameter-scaling analysis. The GENERIC background moved into Appendix B largely retains existing mathematics and is not itself a theoretical addition.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains latent modulation for structure-preserving adaptation without explicit system parameters. However, v2 reframes the abstract and contributions around a systematic Hamiltonian comparison, treating dissipative experiments as additional evidence. It also drops v1's abstract claim of avoiding explicit optimization during adaptation and narrows the conclusion's stated dissipative coverage.

C2.justification: v2 develops new interpretations involving redundant modulation directions, effective rank, alignment with dominant weight-matrix modes, physically structured latent coordinates, and parameter-efficiency tradeoffs. It removes v1's explicit limitations concerning high-dimensional applications and unmeasured computational efficiency, along with the TGC discussion explaining why accurate dynamics need not imply accurate individual physical components.

D1.justification: v2 supplies regularization grids, revised penalty weights, and procedures for basis matching and latent interpolation. However, it omits v1's explicit default latent dimension, GENERIC tensor dimensions, and planned public code-release statement. Hardware, software, optimizer, and much of the training configuration remain documented; neither PDF establishes an available code release.

R1.justification: v2 adds Zintgraf et al. (2019), explicitly connecting latent adaptation to CAVIA, and Hendrycks (2016). Its motivation shifts toward the missing comparison between optimization-based and modulation-based Hamiltonian learning. The existing related-work categories and most cited research remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract and substantial portions of the main narrative are rewritten. Modulation becomes a separate background subsection, problem setup receives its own subsection, GENERIC exposition moves to the appendices, and results are reorganized around efficiency, ablations, and multi-domain learning. The appendices are extensively reorganized, and an impact statement is added.

P2.justification: The main paper changes to a two-column layout. New problem-setup and architecture diagrams accompany numerous sensitivity, efficiency, and latent-space plots. Main tables regroup trajectory and field errors together and separate SSIM; phase-field panels are revised for additional variants and adaptation budgets. The original trajectory-time plot and TGC visualizations are removed.

improvement.justification: The component ablations and representation analyses in v2 Appendix H give better support for design choices that v1 largely left untested, while the new diagrams clarify the method. The overall gain is limited by removed benchmark coverage and limitations, omitted implementation defaults, and conflicting activation and adaptation settings. Revised scores alone do not establish improvement because the experimental protocols changed.
